extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (mentees), potential mentors, host organizations, and journal editors interested in training and mentoring peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A cohort-based or self-guided training program and workshop that teaches early-career researchers how to write constructive manuscript and preprint reviews while centering equity, diversity, and inclusion, and prepares them to become mentors and trained reviewers for editorial prospecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give clear, constructive, and actionable feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: To know how to give clear, constructive, and actionable feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a primary learning objective and emphasized in Module 2 (Reviewer Guide walk-through: Six steps to writing a peer review). The program output expects publication-ready collaborative and individual reviews; instructional materials (Reviewer Guide) and mentorship aim to improve clarity, constructiveness, and actionability of comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand how systems of oppression manifest in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: To know how systems of oppression manifest in the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning objective across modules and cohort curriculum. Participants are taught to recognize structural and systemic issues that influence reviewer selection, evaluation, and outcomes; program stresses continual reassessment to avoid reproducing those systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and address biases in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: To know how to identify and address biases in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly taught in learning objectives and Module 2 (Assessing and addressing biases in peer review). Paired with the Bias Reflection Guide and Review Assessment Rubric to help reviewers examine personal and systemic bias when evaluating manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a manuscript review for a journal or preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: To know how to write a manuscript review for a journal or self-organized review of a preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning objective and practical outcome: participants complete assignments including reading preprints and producing reviews. Module structure (Reviewer Guide, six-step approach) and mentorship support aim to develop the skill of composing full manuscript reviews suitable for journals or public preprint reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage in open peer review of preprints and build a public reviewer profile
rubrics_metrics.description: To know how to engage in the open peer review of preprints and build a public profile as a reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 3 produces collaborative preprint reviews published under CC-BY 4.0 on PREreview.org (DOI via Zenodo). Participants are guided on publishing reviews, obtaining badges/certificates, and using PREreview.org to build visibility for editorial prospecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the 'Six steps to writing a peer review' (Reviewer Guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Reviewer Guide's six-step process to structure manuscript reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 walks through the Reviewer Guide. While the page doesn't list the six steps, it frames them as the core practical methodology for composing reviews, used in assignments and mentorship feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use non-violent communication and conflict resolution in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply elements of non-violent communication and conflict resolution when composing and discussing reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 includes training on non-violent communication and conflict resolution to ensure reviews and reviewer interactions remain respectful and constructive, especially in public/open contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce publishable collaborative and individual preprint reviews (CC-BY 4.0, DOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guided live collaborative reviews and mentee reviews should be published openly under CC-BY 4.0 with DOI assignment via Zenodo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 3 outputs include publication of collaborative reviews; Module 4 (optional mentorship) outputs include published mentee reviews, mentor recognition, and DOI/badge metadata. This sets a standard for openness, attribution, and reproducibility of review outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor qualification: mentors must attend Modules 1 and 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors need to have attended Module 1 and 2 in order to qualify for mentoring roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 4 specifies that mentors must complete foundational workshop modules before mentoring to ensure consistent baseline training in methods, bias recognition, and reviewer guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor practices: create a supportive, nurturing, and safe mentoring space
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors should foster supportive, nurturing, and safe spaces for mentees to develop reviewing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mentor Thought Exercise (recorded video) is used to encourage mentors to adopt these practices before one-on-one calls; guidance emphasized in self-guided component for mentor-mentee interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 completion requirement: publish 2 preprint reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 Review Trainees (RTs) upon completion will have published 2 preprint reviews on PREreview.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit milestone for novice trainees to establish an open review profile and demonstrate basic competency in composing and publishing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 completion requirement: publish 4 additional preprint reviews (total of 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2 Advanced Review Trainees (ARTs) upon completion will have published an additional 4 preprint reviews on PREreview.org, building toward a total of 6 reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outputs are used to build a reviewer profile; completion of Stage 2 positions participants for editorial prospecting and for qualification to Stage 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trained Reviewer list qualification: six highly scored manuscript reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: With a total of 6 highly scored manuscript reviews, ARTs will be added to a Trained Reviewer list for editorial prospecting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page implies reviews are assessed/scored (via the Review Assessment Rubric or other measures) and that high-scoring reviews are a criterion for being recommended to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 3 requirement: completed at least 6 manuscript reviews and mentor ARTs
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 3 Advanced Reviewers (ARs) should have completed at least 6 manuscript reviews and develop mentoring skills by supporting ARTs in the self-guided component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 3 prepares participants to be added to the Trained Reviewer list (if not already) and to transition toward mentorship roles; focus includes implicit bias elements and mentoring practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 4 (Review Mentors) criteria: experienced reviewers or completed Stage 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 4 Review Mentors are experienced reviewers who have either completed Stage 3 or enter with extensive peer review experience (e.g., journal editors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 4 participants mentor Stage 1 trainees in the cohort-based program; they are expected to model best practices and volunteer time to train RTs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias Reflection Guide and Review Assessment Rubric as foundational resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The coursework foundation includes a Reviewer Guide, a Bias Reflection Guide, and a Review Assessment Rubric (available on Zenodo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources are core instructional materials: the Bias Reflection Guide supports bias-awareness work; the Review Assessment Rubric provides criteria/metrics by which reviews are judged (used implicitly for scoring and feedback), and the Reviewer Guide teaches the six-step review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop ability to remain objective by recognizing and challenging internal biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Help mentees recognize and challenge their own internal biases that may influence their ability to remain objective when reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cohort curriculum emphasizes exercises and mentorship to surface and mitigate personal biases as part of producing fair and rigorous reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community and communication competencies for reviewer development
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in community calls, peer-to-peer support chats, and one-to-one mentor/mentee calls as part of reviewer training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cohort-based experience uses social learning and communication channels to develop reviewing skills; active participation in these components is treated as part of training quality and progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and cultural-context considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop content is delivered in English and includes automated closed-captioning; program materials were developed in North America and should be adapted to local cultural contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts can request live-caption/ASL services; program encourages adaptation of curriculum for global audiences and partnering with local organizations to avoid cultural bias and increase relevance.
